newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine business poll shows 66 pct expect growth.
newsitem.headline: Argentine business poll shows 66 pct expect growth.

text.p: A survey of 157 Argentine business leaders published Friday showed 62 percent believe the economy has improved in the past six months and 66 percent expect it to pick up further over the coming half-year.

Polled at the Institute of Business Development's annual conference in Bariloche, only one in 10 business leaders said the economy had got or would get worse. Industry and services were the most optimistic, with 69 percent saying the outlook was bright, versus just 43 percent in agro industry.

Asked about their sector, 48 percent said business had improved in the past half-year and 57 percent expected it to pick up in the coming six months. Only 15 percent said it had got worse and seven percent said it would go downhill.

The business leaders forecast most of their profit growth would come from cost-cutting via new technology, with domestic demand in second place and exports, especially to Mercosur partners Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay, in third place.
But the survey showed that "for half of the businessmen consulted, operations in the Mercosur context are scarce and not yet reflected in their revenue."

Asked what proportion of their sales were generated in the "Southern Cone", which includes Mercosur associate partner Chile, only eight percent said over half their revenue came from the region and 22 percent said it was between a tenth and a third. For 32 percent it was less than a tenth of sales.
